thread:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for service=frontend-api rev=sha-8f3d2a (canary 5%)
monitoring: Alert: 5xx spike > 10% on /v1/generate from us-east-1 (last 2m)
incident-bot: paging @oncall
sam: I'm on it. seeing 5xxs from canary pods. pulling logs now.
sam: logs show image pulled sha-8f3d2a but runtime layer mismatch: "incompatible symbol lookup" in libinference.so
jen: wait, that rev was built with the new base-image digest. CI may have reused an older base layer due to cache.
alex: @sam can you confirm the image digest vs expected? `crane digest gcr.io/redwood/frontend-api:sha-8f3d2a`
sam: `digest=sha256:deadbeef1234` expected `sha256:c0ffee000abc` — mismatch
priya: looks like CI pushed manifest that referenced a cached base layer tag `redwood/base:latest` which got rotated. possible cache poisoning in buildkit remote cache.
mari: paging infra team @alex-infra
alex: assigning to me. rolling canary back to previous stable rev=sha-7e2b1c. Initiating rollback now.
alex: `redwoodctl deploy rollback --service frontend-api --to-revision sha-7e2b1c --scope canary`
deploy-bot: Rollback job kicked. canary scale to previous revision.
sam: doing quick health check... 5xx rate dropping, latency back to normal for canary replicas replaced.
monitoring: 5xx spike mitigated — returning to baseline
jen: we should kill the feature flag that routes traffic to canary while we investigate. Which flag controls this? `feature:frontend_canary_route`
sam: disabling flag now -> `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/flags/frontend_canary_route/disable -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"`
flags-bot: frontend_canary_route disabled by sam
priya: customer impact: loss of requests for ~3m, affected ~0.8% of traffic, mainly from US-EAST. No data exfil.
mari: noted: support/escalation: open incident ticket INC-2026 and notify CS for top 10 affected customers.
jen: adding runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cicd-cache-poisoning|CI/CD cache poisoning runbook>
alex: initial hypothesis: buildkit remote cache returned a deprecated base image digest mapping for `redwood/base:latest` during image manifest creation. This produced a manifest that references incompatible layer set.
sam: steps taken: rolled canary back, disabled canary flag, paged infra, created ticket.
alex: next: need to invalidate remote cache, run full rebuild of affected images with `--no-cache`, and add digest pinning in CI. I'll schedule a patch.
jen: can we re-run CI for rev sha-8f3d2a with `--no-cache` and push a corrected manifest to staging only? keep production pinned until validated.
alex: yes. starting rebuild job: `ci-run --repo frontend-api --revision sha-8f3d2a --no-cache --publish-to staging`
sam: handing off oncall to jen for post-rollback monitoring and customer comms. @jen you're oncall until 17:00 UTC.
jen: ack. I'll watch dashboards and coordinate with CS. Preparing status note for impacted customers.
priya: timeline to include in postmortem: 00:00 deploy start, 00:02 monitoring alert, 00:04 rollback decision, 00:06 rollback complete, 00:08 flag disabled, 00:20 rebuild started.
mari: assigning follow-ups: (1) infra to add cache poisoning detection (alex), (2) CI to enforce digest pinning (devex team - jen), (3) support to notify customers (priya).
sam: thanks all. tagging this for incident review. we'll fill incident template and schedule postmortem at 48h.
jen: status note drafted and sent to CS. monitoring looks stable. closing page but keeping thread open for updates.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 created and linked to this thread
alex: after-action: setting temporary policy: disable use of `:latest` in base images for builds and add digest pin enforcement in CI lint step.
sam: end of on-call shift, handing off final: jen remains primary. good job everyone :thumbsup: 
jen: thanks — will follow up with a small postmortem and remediation PRs.
